title: Energy Flow and Trophic Structure in a Lake Ecosystem

stimulus.title: Energy Content at Each Trophic Level of a Lake Food Chain

prompt: A team of limnologists measured the energy content at each trophic level of a lake food chain over one growing season, shown in the table. The lake has recently experienced increased agricultural runoff from surrounding farmland.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, calculate the percentage of energy transferred from the primary consumer (zooplankton) level to the secondary consumer (minnows) level. Show your work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Identify the general ecological principle illustrated by the pattern of energy values shown in the table, and explain why this pattern occurs in terms of energy use by organisms at each trophic level.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The increased agricultural runoff introduces excess nitrogen and phosphorus into the lake. Describe ONE likely effect this nutrient input will have on the phytoplankton population, and explain ONE consequence this effect could have for dissolved oxygen levels in the lake.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Propose ONE specific, realistic management strategy that could reduce nutrient runoff from the surrounding farmland into the lake, and explain how this strategy would reduce the amount of nitrogen or phosphorus entering the water.

title: Nutrient Cycling and Deforestation in a Tropical Watershed

stimulus.title: Stream Nitrate Concentration Before and After Deforestation

prompt: A watershed research station monitored nitrate concentrations in a stream draining a tropical forest catchment. In year 0, approximately 60% of the forest in the catchment was clear-cut for agriculture. The graph shows nitrate concentrations in the stream from two years before to three years after the deforestation event.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the trend in stream nitrate concentration shown in the graph before and after deforestation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the ecological mechanism by which removing forest vegetation causes an increase in nitrate leaching into the stream.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Identify ONE likely ecological consequence of sustained high nitrate concentrations for organisms living downstream in the river or a receiving lake, and explain the mechanism causing this consequence.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Describe ONE land-use practice the local government could require of farmers in the newly cleared catchment to reduce nitrate export to the stream, and explain how it would reduce nitrogen loss specifically.

title: Comparing Net Primary Productivity Across Biomes

stimulus.title: Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of Four Biomes
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data based on textbook-standard relative NPP rankings

prompt: The bar graph shows average net primary productivity (NPP) for four terrestrial biomes. A student claims that biomes with higher annual temperatures always have higher NPP, based on the fact that the tropical rainforest has the highest NPP of the four biomes shown.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Define net primary productivity (NPP) and explain how it differs from gross primary productivity (GPP).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the graph, evaluate whether the student's claim that higher temperature always leads to higher NPP is well supported. Reference the desert biome specifically in your response.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain ONE reason why temperate grassland has lower NPP than temperate deciduous forest, despite both biomes existing in similar temperature ranges.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain how a multi-year drought would likely affect NPP in the temperate grassland biome shown in the graph, and identify ONE trophic-level consequence of this change for herbivores that depend on grassland vegetation.

title: Island Biogeography and Habitat Fragmentation in a National Park

stimulus.title: Forest Fragment Characteristics and Bird Species Richness

prompt: A national park was subdivided by road construction and agricultural development into four forest fragments of varying size and distance from the nearest large area of continuous forest. Ecologists surveyed bird species richness in each fragment, shown in the table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the theory of island biogeography, explain why Fragment D has much lower bird species richness than Fragment A.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Compare Fragment B and Fragment C. Both differ in one major variable each from Fragment A. Using the data, identify which variable (area or distance) appears to have a stronger relationship with species richness in this data set, and justify your answer using specific values from the table.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe ONE specific conservation strategy that could increase species richness in Fragment D without changing its size, and explain the ecological mechanism by which it would help.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain ONE tradeoff that might make constructing a habitat corridor difficult or costly for the park to implement.

title: Ecological Succession After a Wildfire

stimulus.title: Vegetation Cover and Soil Organic Matter After a Wildfire

prompt: A temperate forest experienced a severe wildfire that killed most above-ground vegetation but left the soil and root systems of some plants intact. Ecologists monitored the site's recovery over 60 years, recording the data in the table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify whether this scenario represents primary or secondary succession, and justify your answer using evidence from the scenario description.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, describe the relationship between time since the fire and soil organic matter, and explain the biological process most responsible for this trend.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why grasses and herbs, rather than mature trees, were the dominant vegetation type just 3 years after the fire.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Predict how species diversity of birds would likely change between year 3 and year 60 of this succession, and explain your reasoning in terms of habitat structure.

title: Ecosystem Services and Coral Reef Degradation

stimulus.title: Coral Reef Condition and Associated Economic Value

prompt: A coastal coral reef ecosystem has degraded significantly between 1990 and 2020 due to warming ocean temperatures, coastal development, and overfishing. The table summarizes changes in reef condition and associated economic indicators over this period.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, identify and classify TWO different ecosystem services provided by the coral reef, one from the provisioning category and one from the regulating category. Justify each classification using specific data from the table.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the ecological mechanism by which declining live coral cover leads to reduced fish catch.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A coastal city is deciding whether to invest $10 million in coral reef restoration or in constructing an artificial seawall for storm protection. Using the concept of ecosystem services, explain ONE advantage that reef restoration might have over the seawall in terms of the range of benefits it provides.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Identify ONE specific human activity contributing to coral reef decline described in the scenario, and propose ONE realistic policy or management action that could directly reduce that specific threat.

title: Age Structure and Population Momentum in Country X

stimulus.title: Age Structure Diagram for Country X

prompt: Country X is a developing nation whose age structure diagram is shown in the bar graph. The country's total fertility rate (TFR) has recently declined to 2.1, the replacement-level fertility rate, due to a successful national family planning and girls' education initiative launched 15 years ago.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the overall shape of Country X's age structure diagram and identify what type of population growth pattern (rapid growth, slow growth, zero growth, or decline) this shape is typically associated with.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Even though Country X's TFR has now reached replacement level (2.1), explain why the country's total population is still likely to continue growing substantially for the next few decades.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain ONE way that the girls' education initiative likely contributed to the decline in total fertility rate over the past 15 years.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Identify ONE specific socioeconomic challenge Country X may face over the next 15 years as a result of the large youth cohort (ages 0-14) shown in the diagram, and explain the mechanism behind this challenge.

title: Survivorship Curves and Conservation Strategy for a Sea Turtle Population

stimulus.title: Survivorship Curve for a Sea Turtle Population
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data illustrating a Type III survivorship pattern
stimulus.yLabel: Number of survivors (log scale, per 1,000 eggs)

prompt: Researchers studying an endangered sea turtle population constructed the survivorship curve shown, based on tracking a cohort of 1,000 eggs from nesting beaches. Adult female turtles nest every 2-3 years, laying approximately 100 eggs per nest, and can live 60-80 years once they reach adulthood.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify the type of survivorship curve (I, II, or III) shown in the graph, and justify your answer using specific data from the graph.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain ONE life-history reason why sea turtles have evolved to produce approximately 100 eggs per nest rather than investing heavily in a small number of offspring.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A conservation organization with limited funding must choose between funding (1) predator-exclusion fencing around nesting beaches to protect eggs and hatchlings, or (2) a program that increases the survival of adult turtles caught incidentally in fishing nets (bycatch). Using the survivorship curve, evaluate which strategy would likely have a greater impact on long-term population growth, and justify your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Identify ONE assumption the researchers made in constructing this survivorship curve from a single cohort of 1,000 eggs, and explain why this assumption could limit the accuracy of the curve.

title: Carrying Capacity and Resource Limitation in a Reintroduced Herbivore Population

stimulus.title: Elk Population Size Following Reintroduction to a Protected Area

prompt: Thirty elk were reintroduced to a protected grassland area with no natural predators present. Wildlife managers tracked the population over the following 30 years, shown in the graph. Vegetation surveys show that available forage biomass per elk declined substantially between years 10 and 20.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify the overall shape of the population growth curve shown in the graph, and state the name of this general growth model.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the graph, estimate the approximate carrying capacity (K) of the elk population in this protected area, and explain how you determined this value from the graph.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why the elk population size decreased slightly between year 20 and year 25, using the vegetation survey information provided in the scenario.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: The protected area has no natural predators. Propose ONE realistic wildlife management strategy to prevent the elk population from once again overshooting carrying capacity and degrading vegetation, and explain how your strategy would help maintain population size near carrying capacity.

title: ENSO Cycles and the Peruvian Anchoveta Fishery

stimulus.title: Sea Surface Temperature Anomaly and Anchoveta Catch off Peru
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data illustrating a typical ENSO cycle and its fishery impacts

prompt: The table above shows sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies off the coast of Peru and the corresponding annual anchoveta (a small forage fish) catch over a five-year period that included both a La Niña event (Year 2) and an El Niño event (Year 4). Peru's anchoveta fishery is one of the largest single-species fisheries in the world and supports both local food security and a major fishmeal export industry.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify the general trend shown in the data between SST anomaly and anchoveta catch, and propose a testable hypothesis that could explain this relationship.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the oceanographic mechanism by which an El Niño event leads to reduced anchoveta catch off the coast of Peru.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe ONE economic or social consequence for Peru of a strong El Niño year, and explain ONE strategy the Peruvian fishing industry could adopt to reduce its vulnerability to future ENSO-driven catch fluctuations.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: A policy maker claims that setting a fixed annual catch quota (the same numeric limit every year regardless of ENSO phase) is the best way to protect the anchoveta population long term. Evaluate this claim using evidence from the table, and explain one limitation of a fixed quota approach.

title: Land Use and Watershed Hydrology

stimulus.title: Peak Stream Discharge Following a 5 cm Storm Event, by Watershed Land Cover

prompt: The bar graph above shows the peak stream discharge recorded in four watersheds of similar size and total rainfall (5 cm) but different dominant land cover, following the same storm event. A rapidly growing suburb is planning to convert a currently forested watershed (similar to the 'Forested' watershed shown) into new suburban housing developments over the next 20 years.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the relationship between impervious surface cover and peak stream discharge shown in the graph.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain TWO specific mechanisms by which converting forested land to suburban development increases peak stream discharge during a storm event.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Identify and explain ONE downstream environmental consequence of the increased peak discharge that would result from this land-use conversion.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Propose ONE specific green infrastructure or land-use planning strategy the suburb could implement to reduce the hydrological impact of the development, and explain how it addresses the mechanism(s) described in part (b).

title: Soil Horizons and Erosion Following Deforestation

stimulus.title: Soil Properties in a Forested Plot vs. an Adjacent Clearcut Plot (Same Slope, 3 Years After Cutting)

prompt: The table above compares soil properties measured in an intact forest plot and an adjacent clearcut plot of the same slope and soil type, three years after the clearcut plot was logged. Researchers are studying the long-term effects of clearcutting on soil formation and stability in this region.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify which soil horizon is most directly represented by the 'A-horizon depth' measurement, and describe one characteristic of this horizon that makes it important for plant growth.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, explain how the loss of organic matter in the clearcut plot is connected to its lower infiltration rate and higher soil loss compared to the forested plot.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why soil formation is generally considered a process that operates on a much longer timescale than soil erosion, and describe why this matters for the long-term recovery of the clearcut plot.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Propose ONE land management practice that could have been used during or after the logging operation to reduce soil erosion, and explain the mechanism by which it would reduce soil loss.

title: Open-Access Fisheries and the Tragedy of the Commons

stimulus.title: Fishing Fleet Size and Fish Population in an Open-Access Coastal Fishery
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data illustrating tragedy-of-the-commons dynamics in a fishery

prompt: The graph above shows the number of fishing boats operating in an open-access coastal fishery (one with no government-enforced catch limits or entry restrictions) and the estimated fish population over a 20-year period. Any fisher may enter the fishery and catch as many fish as they can, and no individual fisher owns the fish stock.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the data, describe the relationship between fleet size and fish population from Year 0 to Year 15, and explain why fleet size declines after Year 15 even though fishing had been unrestricted throughout.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain, using the concept of the tragedy of the commons, why individual fishers in this open-access system continued to enter the fishery and increase fishing effort even as the population was visibly declining.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe ONE specific policy mechanism that could prevent this kind of fishery collapse, and explain how it addresses the underlying open-access problem identified in part (b).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Identify ONE potential economic or social trade-off of implementing the policy mechanism you described in part (c).

title: Comparing Conventional and Sustainable Agricultural Systems

stimulus.title: Five-Year Comparison of a Conventional Monoculture Farm and a Diversified Sustainable Farm

prompt: The table above compares a conventional monoculture corn farm and a diversified sustainable farm (using crop rotation, cover cropping, and integrated pest management) over the same five-year period, which included one severe drought year. Both farms are the same size and located in the same region.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify ONE metric in the table for which the conventional farm outperforms the sustainable farm, and ONE metric for which the sustainable farm outperforms the conventional farm.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the sustainable farm's yield declined much less than the conventional farm's yield during the drought year, connecting your answer to the soil organic matter data in the table.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain how crop rotation, one practice used on the sustainable farm, contributes to both the lower synthetic fertilizer use AND the lower number of pesticide applications shown in the table.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: A farming cooperative is deciding which system to adopt region-wide. Using evidence from the table, argue for ONE system and explain ONE limitation or risk of your recommended system that the cooperative should also consider.

title: Urbanization, Impervious Surfaces, and Stormwater Management

stimulus.title: Watershed Impervious Surface Cover vs. Annual Flood Events (12 Sub-Watersheds)

prompt: The scatter plot above shows the relationship between impervious surface cover and the number of annual flood events across twelve sub-watersheds in a rapidly growing metropolitan region. City planners are deciding whether to approve a new development that would increase impervious surface cover in one currently low-impervious watershed from 20% to an estimated 65%.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the relationship shown in the scatter plot and use it to predict the approximate change in annual flood events if the watershed's impervious cover increases from 20% to 65% as planned.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the physical mechanism by which increasing impervious surface cover leads to more frequent flood events.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Recommend TWO specific green stormwater infrastructure practices the developer could incorporate into the new development to reduce its flood impact, and explain how each addresses the mechanism from part (b).

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Identify ONE reason city planners might still choose to approve high-density development in this watershed despite the flood risk, and explain the environmental trade-off involved.

title: Comparing Lifecycle Emissions and Reliability of Electricity Sources

stimulus.title: Comparison of Electricity Sources for a Regional Grid Planning Decision
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data based on general ranges reported in energy source comparisons

prompt: A regional utility company is deciding how to replace an aging coal power plant that currently provides reliable baseload electricity for the region. The table above compares lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions, capacity factor (percentage of time a source can generate at maximum output), and levelized cost for five electricity sources under consideration.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, identify which source has the lowest lifecycle emissions AND explain why 'lifecycle' emissions are a more complete measure than emissions released only during electricity generation (operation).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why capacity factor is an important consideration for replacing a baseload coal plant, and identify which renewable source in the table would require additional infrastructure (such as storage or backup generation) to reliably replace baseload power.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A community stakeholder argues the utility should choose based on cost alone and select natural gas, since it has the lowest levelized cost among the fossil and low-emission options with high capacity factor. Evaluate this argument by identifying ONE limitation of using levelized cost alone as the deciding factor.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Propose a combination of at least two sources from the table that could replace the coal plant while balancing low emissions and reliability, and justify your choice using specific data from the table.

title: Global Energy Consumption and Development

stimulus.title: Per Capita Energy Consumption in Three Country Groups, 1990-2020
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data illustrating general patterns in global per-capita energy consumption

prompt: The graph above shows per capita energy consumption from 1990 to 2020 for three groups of countries classified by income level. High-income countries have historically consumed the most energy per person, but upper-middle-income countries have shown rapid growth in energy consumption over this period, while low-income countries remain far below both groups.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe ONE notable trend for each of the three country income groups shown in the graph from 1990 to 2020.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain ONE plausible driver of the rapid increase in per capita energy consumption in upper-middle-income countries over this period.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain ONE reason the slight decline in high-income country per capita energy consumption after 2000 does NOT necessarily mean those countries' total environmental impact from energy use has decreased.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: If low-income countries were to raise their per capita energy consumption to match that of upper-middle-income countries primarily using fossil fuels, describe ONE global environmental consequence, and propose ONE strategy that could allow low-income countries to raise energy consumption while limiting that consequence.

title: Energy Efficiency Calculations and Household Conservation

stimulus.title: Household Energy Audit: Baseline Usage and Proposed Upgrades

prompt: The table above shows the results of an energy audit for a household with a total baseline annual electricity consumption of 15,000 kWh, broken down by category, along with the expected percentage reduction in each category if the household adopts the proposed upgrades.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the annual kWh reduction in space heating/cooling energy use if the household adopts the proposed upgrade, and calculate the household's new annual space heating/cooling energy use after the upgrade. Show your work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the household's total annual energy use after ALL FOUR proposed upgrades are implemented, and calculate the overall percentage reduction in total household energy use. Show your work.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Distinguish between energy conservation and energy efficiency, and classify TWO of the four upgrades in the table as primarily reflecting one or the other, with justification.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain why reducing a household's direct electricity consumption, as shown in this audit, may not proportionally reduce that household's greenhouse gas emissions by the same percentage, referencing the source of the region's electricity.

title: Photochemical Smog and Thermal Inversion in a Mountain-Valley City

stimulus.title: Air Quality Data for Valleyview City, Summer Week

prompt: Valleyview City is located in a mountain valley and experiences heavy vehicle traffic each morning. The table above shows morning nitrogen oxide (NOx) concentrations and afternoon ground-level ozone concentrations on five summer days, along with the day's general weather conditions. City officials want to understand why some days have much worse air quality than others and are considering policy responses.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, describe the relationship between the presence of a thermal inversion and afternoon ground-level ozone concentrations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the atmospheric mechanism by which a thermal inversion contributes to elevated ground-level ozone and other pollutant concentrations in a valley city.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe the two-step chemical process by which NOx and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) form ground-level ozone in the presence of sunlight.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Propose one specific policy or technological solution the city could implement to reduce morning NOx emissions, and describe one potential economic or social tradeoff associated with your proposed solution.

title: Acid Deposition and Lake Ecosystem Recovery

stimulus.title: Lake pH and Fish Population Index, 1970-2020
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data for this exercise, modeled on documented acid rain recovery trends following the 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments

prompt: The graph shows changes in the pH and fish population index of a temperate lake downwind of a coal-burning region from 1970 to 2020. The 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments established a cap-and-trade program that significantly reduced SO2 emissions from power plants beginning in the early 1990s.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify the trend in lake pH from 1970 to 1990, and describe the corresponding trend in the fish population index over the same period.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the chemical process by which SO2 emissions from coal-burning power plants lead to the acidification of a lake located downwind.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Using evidence from the graph, explain how the 1990 Clean Air Act Amendments likely contributed to the recovery of lake pH and fish populations after 1990.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Describe one direct chemical/physical intervention (other than reducing emissions) that resource managers could use to raise the pH of an acidified lake, and explain one limitation of this approach compared to reducing emissions at the source.

title: Indoor Air Quality and the Energy Efficiency Tradeoff

stimulus.title: Indoor Pollutant Concentrations in Homes with Standard vs. Airtight (Weatherized) Construction

prompt: A city is offering rebates to homeowners who weatherize (seal air leaks and add insulation) their homes to reduce heating and cooling energy consumption. The graph shows measured indoor radon and formaldehyde concentrations in a sample of standard homes compared to airtight, weatherized homes in the same region.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the pattern shown in the graph comparing pollutant concentrations in standard versus airtight homes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why weatherizing a home to improve energy efficiency tends to increase concentrations of indoor air pollutants such as radon and formaldehyde.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe the specific health risk associated with long-term radon exposure, including the biological mechanism of harm.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Propose a specific mitigation strategy the city could recommend alongside its weatherization rebate program to prevent the buildup of indoor air pollutants, and explain how it addresses the tradeoff identified in part (b).

title: Eutrophication and the Oxygen Sag Curve Downstream of a Wastewater Outfall

stimulus.title: Dissolved Oxygen and Biological Oxygen Demand Downstream of a Wastewater Treatment Outfall
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data for this exercise, illustrating a classic oxygen sag curve

prompt: A wastewater treatment plant discharges partially treated effluent into a river. The graph shows dissolved oxygen (DO) and biological oxygen demand (BOD) at increasing distances downstream from the outfall.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the relationship between BOD and dissolved oxygen concentration shown in the graph as distance downstream increases.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the biological mechanism that causes dissolved oxygen to decline near the outfall despite the river not having a direct source of an oxygen-depleting chemical.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Identify one aquatic organism or group of organisms that would likely experience population decline in the reach of river between 2 and 10 km downstream, and justify your answer using the graph.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Propose one specific upgrade to the wastewater treatment process that would reduce the severity of the oxygen sag shown in the graph, and explain the mechanism by which it would help.

title: Biomagnification of Mercury in an Estuarine Food Web

stimulus.title: Mercury Concentration at Successive Trophic Levels in an Estuary

prompt: An industrial facility upstream of an estuary historically released mercury-contaminated wastewater. Researchers sampled tissue from organisms at each trophic level of the estuarine food web and recorded the mercury concentrations shown in the table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, calculate the factor by which mercury concentration increased from small fish (minnows) to the osprey.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the biological process responsible for the pattern of increasing mercury concentration shown in the table, and describe why mercury is particularly prone to this process compared to a water-soluble, easily excreted compound.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe one specific human health risk associated with consuming top-predator fish species like bass from this estuary, and identify one population that is at elevated risk.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Identify a possible remediation or management solution to reduce human exposure risk from this contaminated food web, and describe one economic or social tradeoff of your proposed solution.

title: Dose-Response Relationships and Pesticide Risk Assessment

stimulus.title: Dose-Response Curve for Pesticide X in a Laboratory Test Population

prompt: Toxicologists exposed a test population of laboratory animals to varying doses of Pesticide X and recorded the percent mortality at each dose, shown in the graph. Regulators are using this dose-response data to help set a legal exposure limit for agricultural workers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the graph, identify the approximate LD50 for Pesticide X and explain what this value represents.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Describe the general shape of the curve shown in the graph and explain what this shape indicates about the relationship between dose and toxicity for most substances.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A farmworker is regularly exposed to low doses of Pesticide X that would each individually cause less than 5% mortality risk in this dataset. Explain why regulators might still be concerned about this worker's long-term health, referencing the concept of chronic toxicity.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Propose one specific policy that regulators could implement to protect agricultural workers from long-term Pesticide X exposure, and explain how it directly reduces exposure risk.

title: Stratospheric Ozone Recovery and the Montreal Protocol

stimulus.title: Antarctic Ozone Hole Maximum Area, 1980-2020
stimulus.sourceNote: Approximate values based on NASA/NOAA satellite ozone monitoring records

prompt: The graph shows the maximum area of the Antarctic ozone hole from 1980 to 2020. The Montreal Protocol, an international treaty phasing out the production of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and other ozone-depleting substances, was signed in 1987 and has been amended and strengthened several times since.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the overall trend in ozone hole area shown in the graph from 1980 to 2006, and the trend from 2006 to 2020.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the chemical mechanism by which CFCs released at Earth's surface lead to the destruction of stratospheric ozone.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Using the graph, explain why the ozone hole did not immediately shrink after the Montreal Protocol was signed in 1987, even though it continued to grow for nearly two more decades.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Describe one specific consequence to human health OR ecosystems that results from increased UV radiation reaching Earth's surface due to ozone depletion, and explain the mechanism of harm.

title: Ocean Acidification, Coral Calcification, and Reef Ecosystem Impacts

stimulus.title: Coral Calcification Rate vs. Seawater pH
stimulus.sourceNote: Hypothetical data for this exercise, illustrating a pattern consistent with published ocean acidification research

prompt: Ocean surface pH has declined from a pre-industrial average of approximately 8.2 as the ocean has absorbed increasing amounts of atmospheric carbon dioxide. Researchers exposed coral samples to seawater at different pH levels and measured their calcification (skeleton-building) rate relative to the pre-industrial baseline, shown in the scatter plot.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe the relationship between seawater pH and coral calcification rate shown in the scatter plot.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the chemical mechanism by which increasing atmospheric CO2 concentrations lower ocean pH.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why lower pH specifically reduces the ability of corals (and other calcifying organisms) to build calcium carbonate skeletons or shells.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Identify one ecosystem service provided by coral reefs that would be lost or degraded if reef-building slows significantly due to ocean acidification, and explain the connection between reduced calcification and the loss of that service.

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Ocean acidification and ocean warming often occur simultaneously and both stress coral reefs. Explain why addressing only local stressors (such as reducing nutrient runoff or overfishing near a reef) would be insufficient to fully protect coral reefs from these two global stressors.

title: Habitat Fragmentation, Invasive Species, and Biodiversity Loss in a National Park

stimulus.title: Bird Species Richness and Presence of Invasive Predators in Forest Patches

prompt: Ecologists surveyed four forest patches within and around a national park that vary in size, connectivity to other patches via wildlife corridors, and the presence of an invasive predator (a nonnative mammal that preys on ground-nesting birds). Bird species richness was recorded for each patch.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, compare bird species richness between Patch A and Patch B, and propose a hypothesis for why they differ, based only on the variables shown.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain the ecological mechanism by which habitat fragmentation (small, isolated patches) reduces species richness, independent of the effects of invasive species.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Using the data in the table, describe the effect of the invasive predator on bird species richness by comparing patches of similar size and connectivity (Patch A vs. Patch C, and Patch B vs. Patch D).

parts.label: (d)
